subject: HarborBank RFP — provisioning mapping, delegated-admin, and SSO options
messages:
From: Amy Lee <amy.lee@harborbank.com>
To: connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@harborbank.com
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood — questions on IAM section of RFP

Hi Connor,

Thanks for submitting the initial RFP packet. We reviewed the IAM section and have a handful of follow-ups so we can finalize the tech evaluation:

1) SCIM: does Redwood support delta-only SCIM sync and partial attribute patching for large groups? We need to avoid full-group re-provisioning during nightly syncs.
2) Role mapping: can we map SCIM groups to multiple RBAC roles (e.g., group A => roles reader+auditor) and manage precedence rules?
3) Delegated admin: we require delegated admin accounts with constrained scopes and audit logs showing admin actions over a 365-day retention.
4) SSO: we prefer OIDC for newer apps but still require SAML metadata import for older systems. Does Redwood support both for the same account and per-application config?
5) Test tenancy: will we get a staging tenant to validate provisioning workflows before production cutover?

Can you reply with specifics and any templates we should use for group->role mappings? If you prefer, we can do a 30-minute technical call next week.

Appreciate it,
Amy
Amy Lee
Senior Procurement Manager | HarborBank
---
Attachment: harborbank-rfp-iam.pdf (pdf stub)

From: connor_obrien@redwood.ai
To: Amy Lee <amy.lee@harborbank.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood — questions on IAM section of RFP

Hi Amy — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Laura (sales lead) and Neha (identity product SME). Quick answers up front, followed by a short plan and templates attached.

Short answers:
- SCIM: yes — we support delta syncs and PATCH-based attribute updates; we also offer an efficient group sync mode for large directories.
- Role mapping: yes — groups can map to multiple roles and we surface precedence and deny rules.
- Delegated admin: yes — scoped admin roles with audit trails; default audit retention 365 days, configurable longer with add-on.
- SSO: support for both SAML and OIDC; per-application choice and multiple IdPs per org.
- Staging tenant: yes — we provide a timeboxed staging tenant for testing provisioning flows as part of onboarding.

Plan and next steps:
1) I attached a SCIM mapping template (scim_mapping_template.csv) — if you can populate group names + key attributes we’ll draft an initial mapping.
2) Laura will follow up on licensing and timeline for a staging tenant.
3) Neha can host a 30-minute technical session (recommended) to walk the team through delta sync behavior and error handling.

Would Friday 4/8 @10am PT work for a quick call?

Best,
Connor O'Brien
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

Attachments: scim_mapping_template.csv, redwood-iam-capability-matrix.pdf

Connor/Team,

Thanks — a few clarifying items after reviewing the mapping template you sent:

- For extremely large groups (~50k users), can group membership be represented as a pointer (external group id) instead of enumerating members in SCIM push events?
- We have a need for conditional claims in OIDC tokens (e.g., include department claim only for internal services). Can Redwood supply dynamic claim transformations or attribute filters per client?
- When a user is removed from a group, what is the typical time-to-deprovision in production (delta vs full sync)?

Also: procurement needs to confirm audit retention SLA language — can you give the exact retention and export formats (CSV, JSON) and whether logs include admin session IDs for delegated-admin actions?

Thanks,
Daniel

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@harborbank.com>, Amy Lee <amy.lee@harborbank.com>
Cc: connor_obrien@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 6 Apr 2027 09:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood — questions on IAM section of RFP (detailed answers + artifacts)

Hi Daniel / Amy — thanks for the follow-ups. Below are explicit answers and the behavioral/operational details you asked for. I've included links to artifacts in Drive and attached the capability matrix and audit summary PDF.

1) SCIM and large groups
- External group reference: we support representing membership by external group id for partner connectors (SCIM 2.0 extensions + delegated sync), which avoids full member enumeration in every push. For customers using our SSO-only connector, we also provide a "group delta" mode where only adds/removes are transmitted.
- Deprovision timing: in typical production settings with default sync cadence (near-real-time for IdP pushes, configurable polling for inbound syncs), remove events propagate within 30-120 seconds for push-based flows and within 2-15 minutes for polling delta syncs. We can prioritize low-latency deprovisioning in Dedicated deployments.

2) Role mapping and precedence
- Groups->roles: a single SCIM group can map to multiple RBAC roles. The mapping table supports explicit precedence and deny rules; precedence is enforced at evaluation time and documented in the mapping export.
- Role composition: roles are composable and you can create composite roles (e.g., reader + auditor) and assign via group mapping to simplify policy management.

3) Delegated admin and audit logs
- Scoped admin: we provide several built-in delegated admin templates (user-admin, group-admin, billing-admin) and you can author custom admin roles with fine-grained scopes (read/write on specific resources).
- Audit logs: admin actions are logged with actor, session id, action, target resource, pre/post state for config changes where applicable, and correlation id. Default retention is 365 days; exportable formats: JSON lines, CSV, and syslog/SIEM forwarders. Longer retention is available as an add-on.

4) SSO: SAML & OIDC per-app flexibility
- Per-application protocol: each application in the Redwood tenant can be configured independently to use SAML or OIDC, and we support multiple IdPs per org with routing rules.
- Claim transformations: yes — token/attribute pipelines let you conditionally include, rename, or hash attributes. Transformations support regex and simple conditional logic; for complex needs we can add a middleware mapping during onboarding.

5) Additional operational notes
- Rate limits and throttling: SCIM endpoints have tenant-level rate limits (configurable on Dedicated); default for Hosted customers is 600 requests/minute with exponential backoff behaviors documented in our developer portal.
- Test tenant: staging tenants are provisioned during onboarding for 30 days by default; extended sandbox windows can be added per contract.
- Cutover playbook: we'll provide a cutover checklist (pre-provision, test accounts, pilot group, monitoring hooks) and can run a dry-run in your staging tenant.

Next steps we propose:
- Fill and return the attached scim_mapping_template.csv with 2-3 sample groups (we'll do a dry-run mapping).
- Schedule a 30-minute technical session with Neha to walk through delta flow, token claims, and delegated admin audit exports.
- Connor will provide a staging tenant timeline and license notes.

Proposed slot: Friday 4/8 @10am PT — Neha, Connors, can you confirm? Daniel, Amy — does that work?

Best,
Laura Bennett
Head of Strategic Sales | Redwood Inference
